subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
title: Hypertensive disorders: preeclampsia, eclampsia and HELLP

steps.tx: **Preeclampsia** begins after twenty weeks with blood pressure of one hundred and forty over ninety twice plus proteinuria of three hundred milligrams or a protein creatinine ratio of thirty, or thrombocytopenia, renal or liver involvement, pulmonary oedema, headache or visual symptoms. Failed spiral artery remodelling with sFlt-1 and placental growth factor imbalance links it to eclampsia, while chronic hypertension predates twenty weeks. Aspirin one hundred and fifty milligrams from twelve to thirty six weeks prevents disease in high risk women.
steps.say: Preeclampsia is hypertension after twenty weeks with proteinuria or organ dysfunction, and the chart separates it from chronic hypertension before twenty weeks and gestational hypertension without protein. Placental vessels fail to remodel, and angiogenic factors such as sFlt-1 rise. Proteinuria means three hundred milligrams daily or a ratio of thirty, and severe features replace protein at times. High risk women should receive aspirin one hundred and fifty milligrams from twelve to thirty six weeks.

vis.alt: Chronic hypertension predates 20 weeks; gestational starts at or after 20 weeks without proteinuria; preeclampsia starts at or after 20 weeks with 140 over 90 twice plus protein 300 mg per day or PCR 30, or any severe feature. High-risk women take aspirin 150 mg from 12 to 36 weeks.
vis.caption: 20 weeks and proteinuria split the three; aspirin 150 mg prevents.

steps.tx: **Severe preeclampsia** shows headache, visual blurring, an epigastric band from liver capsule stretch, clonus, platelets under one lakh, doubled creatinine, doubled transaminases or pulmonary oedema, and eclampsia adds tonic clonic seizures with risks of posterior reversible encephalopathy and intracerebral bleeding. HELLP syndrome means haemolysis, elevated liver enzymes and low platelets, often with epigastric pain and disseminated intravascular coagulation. Watch brisk reflexes and urine output, and grade vasospasm on fundoscopy, because deterioration can be rapid and delivery planning must not wait for protein alone.
steps.say: Severe disease announces itself with headache, blurred vision, epigastric band pain from the stretched liver capsule, and brisk reflexes with clonus. Blood tests may show platelets under one lakh, doubled creatinine or doubled liver enzymes, and the lungs can fill with pulmonary oedema. Eclampsia adds generalised seizures, while HELLP adds haemolysis with low platelets and a risk of disseminated coagulation. Brisk reflexes, urine output and the fundus all need close watching.

steps.tx: **Magnesium sulphate** prevents and treats eclamptic seizures, loaded as four grams intravenously plus ten grams intramuscularly in the Pritchard regimen then five grams four hourly, or one to two grams hourly in the Zuspan regimen. Toxicity first abolishes reflexes, then depresses breathing and can arrest the heart, and calcium gluconate is the antidote, so reflexes, breathing and urine output gate each dose. Labetalol leads pressure control with nifedipine and hydralazine alternatives, angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors are banned, and fluids stay restricted.
steps.say: Magnesium sulphate is the drug that prevents and stops eclamptic fits, by the Pritchard intramuscular schedule or the Zuspan intravenous infusion shown in the image. Toxicity climbs from lost knee reflexes to slow breathing to cardiac arrest, and calcium gluconate reverses it, so checks of reflexes, respiration and urine output gate every dose. Labetalol controls severe pressure first, with nifedipine or hydralazine as alternatives, while angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitors stay banned.

vis.alt: Pritchard loads 4 g IV plus 10 g IM then 5 g IM 4-hourly; Zuspan loads 4 g IV then 1 to 2 g per hour. Toxicity climbs from lost reflexes to slow breathing to arrest, reversed by calcium gluconate. Labetalol leads pressure control; ACE inhibitors are banned.
vis.caption: Pritchard IM or Zuspan IV; lost reflexes stop the drip.

steps.tx: Delivery is the cure for **preeclampsia**, timed at thirty seven weeks without severe features and thirty four weeks with severe features, and immediately for eclampsia, HELLP, pulmonary oedema, disseminated coagulation or uncontrolled pressure. Vaginal delivery is preferred when stable, while caesarean section serves unfavourable cervix, emergency or fetal compromise, and platelets gate regional anaesthesia. Seizures can still occur forty eight hours postpartum, pressures need review to twelve weeks, and labetalol and nifedipine suit breastfeeding.
steps.say: Only delivery cures preeclampsia, and timing follows severity: thirty seven weeks without severe features, thirty four weeks with them, and immediate delivery for eclampsia, HELLP, pulmonary oedema or uncontrolled pressure. A stable patient can be induced vaginally, while caesarean delivery answers emergency, fetal distress or an unfavourable cervix, and the platelet count decides spinal safety. Fits can still strike forty eight hours after birth, so surveillance continues, and blood pressure is reviewed to twelve weeks.
